arxiv-2109-08992.title: High-Accuracy Absolute Magnetometry with Application to the Fermilab Muon g − 2 g-2 Experiment
arxiv-2109-08992.creator: and P. Winter
arxiv-2109-08992.description: Abstract We present details of a high-accuracy absolute scalar magnetometer based on pulsed proton NMR. The B B -field magnitude is determined from the precession frequency of proton spins in a cylindrical sample of water after accounting for field perturbations from probe materials, sample shape, and other corrections.

arxiv-2202-02864.title: Alpha Blending with No Division Operations
arxiv-2202-02864.creator: Jerry R. Van Aken
arxiv-2202-02864.description: Abstract Highly accurate alpha blending can be performed entirely with integer operations, and no divisions. To reduce the number of integer multiplications, multiple color components can be blended in parallel in the same 32-bit or 64-bit register. This tutorial explains how to avoid division operations when alpha blending with 32-bit RGBA pixels.

arxiv-2202-06129.description: Abstract . With the increasing demands on e-commerce platforms, numerous user action history is emerging. Those enriched action records are vital to understand users’ interests and intents. Recently, prior works for user behavior prediction mainly focus on the interactions with product-side information.

arxiv-2202-11114.title: Twist-three cross-sections in deeply virtual Compton scattering
arxiv-2202-11114.creator: Yuxun Guo, Xiangdong Ji, Brandon Kriesten, and Kyle Shiells
arxiv-2202-11114.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Yuxun Guo, Xiangdong Ji, Brandon Kriesten, and Kyle Shiells. We study the deeply virtual Compton scattering process with both twist-two and twist-three Compton form factors and present our cross-sections formulas with all polarization configurations.

arxiv-2204-07230.title: Learning two-phase microstructure evolution using neural operators and autoencoder architectures
arxiv-2204-07230.creator: Vivek Oommen, Khemraj Shukla, Somdatta Goswami, Rémi Dingreville, George Em Karniadakis
arxiv-2204-07230.description: Abstract Phase-field modeling is an effective but computationally expensive method for capturing the mesoscale morphological and microstructure evolution in materials. Hence, fast and generalizable surrogate models are needed to alleviate the cost of computationally taxing processes such as in optimization and design of materials.

arxiv-2309-11710.title: ContextRef: Evaluating Referenceless Metrics For Image Description Generation
arxiv-2309-11710.creator: Elisa Kreiss, Eric Zelikman, Christopher Potts, Nick Haber {ekreiss, ezelikman, cgpotts, nhaber}@stanford.edu
arxiv-2309-11710.description: Abstract Referenceless metrics (e.g., CLIPScore) use pretrained vision--language models to assess image descriptions directly without costly ground-truth reference texts. Such methods can facilitate rapid progress, but only if they truly align with human preference judgments. In this paper, we introduce ContextRef, a benchmark for assessing referenceless metrics for such alignment.

arxiv-2402-16751.title: Value Preferences Estimation and Disambiguation in Hybrid Participatory Systems
arxiv-2402-16751.creator: Enrico Liscio e.liscio@tudelft.nl, Catholijn M. Jonker c.m.jonker@tudelft.nl, Leiden University, The Netherlands, Pradeep K. Murukannaiah p.k.murukannaiah@tudelft.nl
arxiv-2402-16751.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Enrico Liscio e.liscio@tudelft.nl, Catholijn M. Jonker c.m.jonker@tudelft.nl, Leiden University, The Netherlands, Pradeep K. Murukannaiah p.k.murukannaiah@tudelft.nl. Understanding citizens’ values in participatory systems is crucial for citizen-centric policy-making. We envision a hybrid participatory system where participants make choices and provide motivations for those choices, and AI agents estimate their value preferences by interacting with them. We focus on situations where a conflict is detected between participants’ choices and motivations, and propose methods for estimating value preferences while addressing detected inconsistencies by interacting with the participants.

arxiv-2403-17519.title: Determination of the dynamic Young’s modulus of quantum materials in piezoactuator-driven uniaxial pressure cells using a low-frequency a.c. method
arxiv-2403-17519.creator: Caitlin I. O’Neil 1,2, Zhenhai Hu 1,2, Naoki Kikugawa 3, Dmitry A. Sokolov 1, Andrew P. Mackenzie 1,2, Hilary M. L. Noad 1, Elena Gati 1
arxiv-2403-17519.description: Abstract We report on a new technique for measuring the dynamic Young’s modulus, E E , of quantum materials at low temperatures as a function of static tuning strain, ϵ \epsilon , in piezoactuator-driven pressure cells. In addition to a static tuning of stress and strain, we apply a small-amplitude, finite-frequency a.c.

arxiv-2407-10705.title: Impact of electron spectra on morphology of pulsar halos at ultra-high energies Journal: Journal of High Energy Astrophysics
arxiv-2407-10705.creator: Ying-Ying Guo, Qiang Yuan
arxiv-2407-10705.description: Abstract The extended γ \gamma -ray halos around pulsars are unique probe of transportation of high-energy electrons (and positrons) in vicinities of such pulsars. Observations of morphologies of several such halos indicate that particles diffuse very slowly around pulsars, compared with that in the Milky Way halo.

arxiv-2410-01923.title: On the early thermal processing of planetesimals during and after the giant planet instability
arxiv-2410-01923.creator: Anastasios Gkotsinas, David Nesvorný, Aurélie Guilbert-Lepoutre, Sean N. Raymond, Nathan Kaib
arxiv-2410-01923.description: Abstract Born as ice-rich planetesimals, cometary nuclei were gravitationally scattered onto their current orbits in the Kuiper Belt and the Oort Cloud during the giant planets’ dynamical instability in the early stages of our Solar System’s history. Here, we model the thermal evolution of planetesimals during and after the giant planet instability.

arxiv-2412-20195.title: Lower bounds on transformers with infinite precision
arxiv-2412-20195.creator: Alexander Kozachinskiy
arxiv-2412-20195.description: Abstract In this note, we use the VC dimension technique to prove the first lower bound against one-layer softmax transformers with infinite precision. We do so for two tasks: function composition, considered by Peng, Narayanan, and Papadimitriou, and the SUM 2 task, considered by Sanford, Hsu, and Telgarsky.

arxiv-2506-10903.title: Beyond Gold Standards: Epistemic Ensemble of LLM Judges for Formal Mathematical Reasoning
arxiv-2506-10903.creator: Lan Zhang, Marco Valentino, André Freitas
arxiv-2506-10903.description: Abstract Autoformalization plays a crucial role in formal mathematical reasoning by enabling the automatic translation of natural language statements into formal languages. While recent advances using large language models (LLMs) have shown promising results, methods for automatically evaluating autoformalization remain underexplored. arxiv-2510-06084.title: Spectrum Tuning: Post-Training for Distributional Coverage and In-Context Steerability
arxiv-2510-06084.creator: Taylor Sorensen, Benjamin Newman, Jared Moore, Chan Park, Jillian Fisher, Niloofar Mireshghallah, Liwei Jiang, Yejin Choi
arxiv-2510-06084.description: Abstract Language model post-training has enhanced instruction-following and performance on many downstream tasks, but also comes with an often-overlooked cost on tasks with many possible valid answers. We characterize three desiderata for conditional distributional modeling: in-context steerability, valid output space coverage, and distributional alignment, and document across three model families how current post-training can reduce these properties.

arxiv-2512-08978.title: Institutional AI Sovereignty Through Gateway Architecture: Implementation Report from Fontys ICT
arxiv-2512-08978.creator: Ruud Huijts, Koen Suilen
arxiv-2512-08978.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Ruud Huijts, Koen Suilen. Executive Summary To address the fragmented, high-risk and inequitable adoption of commercial AI tools, we designed and operated an institutional AI platform in a six-month, 300-user pilot. The aim was to demonstrate that a university of applied sciences can offer advanced AI capabilities on its own terms, with fair access for all students and staff, transparent risks, controlled costs and full alignment with European law. Commercial AI subscriptions proved incompatible with that mission.

pmc-10693006.title: Host learning selects for the coevolution of greater egg mimicry and narrower antiparasitic egg-rejection thresholds
pmc-10693006.creator: Kuangyi Xu, Maria R Servedio, Sarah K Winnicki, Csaba Moskat, Jeffrey P Hoover, Abbigail M Turner, Mark E Hauber
pmc-10693006.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Egg rejection is an effective and widespread antiparasitic defense to eliminate foreign eggs from the nests of hosts of brood parasitic birds. Several lines of observational and critical experimental evidence support a role for learning by hosts in the recognition of parasitic versus own eggs; specifically, individual hosts that have had prior or current experience with brood parasitism are more likely to reject foreign eggs.

pmc-13501083.title: Modulating glutamate neurotransmission in in vivo models of Multiple Sclerosis: a narrative review
pmc-13501083.creator: Eleni Stamoula, Theofanis Vavilis, Ioanna Boskou, Olga Vampertzi, Nikoletta Floropoulou, Antonia Demopoulos, Rafaella Grigoriou, Mikhail Melnikov
pmc-13501083.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Glutamate (Glu), the primary excitatory neurotransmitter of the central and peripheral nervous systems, plays essential roles in cognition, synaptic plasticity, and immune modulation. Its dysregulation is increasingly recognized as a component of neuroinflammation and neurodegeneration in multiple sclerosis (MS). In MS and its principal experimental model, experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis (EAE), impaired Glu homeostasis leads to excitotoxicity, calcium overload, and oxidative damage, compounded by proinflammatory mediators such as TNF-α.

pmc-13676277.title: Disease Activity During Pregnancy and Postpartum in Women With Multiple Sclerosis Treated With Ocrelizumab or Rituximab Before Pregnancy
pmc-13676277.creator: Nadine Bast, Karen Dost-Kovalsky, Sabrina Haben, Laura Witt, Ralf Gold, Sandra Thiel, Kerstin Hellwig
pmc-13676277.description: Background and ObjectivesPreliminary data suggest sustained disease control with ocrelizumab (OCR) or rituximab (RTX) in women with multiple sclerosis (MS) after pregnancy suspension; however, the influence of washout duration and cumulative dosing remains unknown. This study investigates disease activity during and after pregnancy in women with relapsing-remitting MS treated with OCR/RTX before pregnancy.

uslaw-usc-t19-s2483.description: United States Code, Title 19 (Customs Duties); Chapter 12 (Trade Act Of 1974); Subchapter VI (General Provisions).
